# Research intraday small-target strategies with causal no-trade rules

## Active claim — 2026-10-24 official calendar renewal

Owner: Codex. Branches: `codex/tokyo-calendar-2027` in core, Strat and hosted
app. The owner requests repair of the December 2026 cutoff. Extend the reviewed
Japanese holiday calendar through the latest officially published full year
(2027), using Cabinet Office dates, including substitute holidays. Preserve
every date and schedule decision in the old coverage. Do not invent unpublished
holidays or remove the out-of-coverage entry guard.

Producer scope: embedded calendar, scheduled-family calendar coverage and tests,
spec, conformance fixtures/goldens only where affected, changelog, immutable
release. Consumer scope: matching calendar and feature-specific scheduled release
pin, audited calendar-only renewal of saved Tokyo paper runs, dynamic coverage
wording, renewal/check tooling or documentation, focused tests and immutable
HT-323 memory. Existing source, schedule, costs, account/credential bindings,
stopped intent, positions, attempted dates and journal history stay protected.
Only the exact reviewed append-only calendar upgrade may migrate automatically;
other identity drift still refuses recovery. Include native/WASM/calendar parity,
2027 holiday/settlement cases, old-date parity, unknown-year refusal and saved-run
renewal/restart tests. Helpers may independently review disjoint calendar and
recovery paths. Parent owns integration, release and hosted verification.

Oracle CI on producer PR152 refused the expected source-inventory drift before
ordinary arithmetic qualification. Extend producer scope to
`scripts/checks/sequential-arithmetic-schedules.json` and a dated calendar
source-review note under `docs/`. Review the changed calendar/conformance source
and embedded-data hashes; regenerate only the matching global inventory and
target dependency closures. Compare every pinned Go 1.22.12 instruction stream
on Linux AMD64, Linux ARM64 and WASM before changing any instruction hash.
Arithmetic inputs, expected leaves, schedules, flags, proof code and admission
checks stay unchanged. Any instruction difference needs a concrete independent
review; do not relax or bypass the proof. Exact-head Oracle CI must pass before
release. This is part of the calendar request, not a new arithmetic feature.

Acceptance: reviewed producer release precedes consumer adoption; relevant local
checks and required Oracle CI pass; app preview is verified before production;
the original hosted paper run retains its ledger and running intent. Record
the new finite official coverage and how to renew it before expiration. No
broker orders or global execution switches are authorized.

## Problem and scope

The owner requested on 2026-10-23 a profitable day-trading candidate from latest
main in an isolated worktree, favouring frequent smaller wins on gold or FX,
with observable rules for when not to trade. A modest profit factor and some
losing years are acceptable. This is a new bounded study, separate from the
three rejected momentum hypotheses recorded by HT-315 and all active producer
language work. Backtests cannot establish future profitability.

## Released claim — 2026-10-23 small-target research

Owner: Codex. Branch: `codex/daytrade-regime-research`, main base
`35cd03c645f88bea4ac4b4113de935ad1cea597c`.
Write scope: `scripts/research/daytrade-regime/`,

`strategies/evidence/daytrade-regime/`, and immutable
`.project-memory/tasks/HT-323/` records. Scratch studies stay outside registration.
Luna helper reviews existing evidence read-only; parent owns all writes.
No existing engine, strategy registry, book, generated atlas, or other owner's
evidence paths may change without a prospective scope update. No live orders,
deployment, credentials, or external paid services are needed.

## Acceptance

- Review prior art and log all tested hypotheses and variants.
- Freeze a chronological development/test split before new outcomes.
- Use completed-bar signals, explicit execution and costs, intraday exits,
  and no filters selected from future outcomes.
- Report hit rate, trade frequency, realistic and stressed cost results,
  year splits, drawdown, losing streaks, and sensitivity to nearby settings.
- Compare the no-trade rule with the ungated baseline and inspect skipped periods.
- Retain runnable candidate and evidence if justified; do not publish a failed
  test as a finished strategy or change book membership.

## Validation

Focused causal/execution tests, reproducible historical runs, `pnpm test` for
strategy or money logic changes, `git diff --check`, and project-memory
validation on the committed implementation head. Record exact commands and
limitations after running them.

## Integration

Research only. Any implementation PR must link this task and retain the full
search record. Forward testing and book membership are separate decisions.

## Review handoff — 2026-10-23

Implementation: [app PR539](https://github.com/spik3r/heisentick/pull/539),
commit `9e7e3857f9cc0e7d69ae17fbe167aa7744f99e5f`. Research editing is

is claimed. The owner/reviewer can assess the evidence before any new paper

The fixed USDJPY settlement-day short has 388 trades, 57.2% wins and PF 1.59
after an assumed 1.5-pip round-trip cost; PF is 1.44 at 2 pips. The final
2025–September 2026 partition has PF 1.34, while partial 2026 alone loses
82.4 pips (4.12R). Non-settlement weekdays lose money (PF 0.85); five minutes
of entry delay removes the edge. Frequency is about 1.3 trades per week.
Known prior history prevents a pristine out-of-sample claim. This is a
positive historical watch candidate with executable live profitability unproven.

Retained evidence: 48 rejected indicator route cells, two Tokyo-fix
candidates and 14 diagnostic configurations; exact trade ledgers, costs,
calendar source, monthly-block bootstrap and source/input hashes. Seven

## Released claim extension — 2026-10-24 bounded static availability admission

The first hosted preview for the reviewed Tokyo consumer reached Cloudflare's
deployment-stage success state, but its first immutable public static GET
returned HTTP 500; later GETs to the same deployment URL returned the expected
bytes. Extend the app follow-up to address this control-plane/data-plane gap
without publishing again or weakening static-byte acceptance. Work in
`Heisentick/heisentick-app`, branch `codex/tokyo-static-availability`, based on
app main `185567005cc8c106ddaf6ec7652a1680ba2dedf7`.

Write scope remains `scripts/deploy/frontendPages.mjs`,
`test/frontendDeploymentPipeline.test.mjs`, and immutable
`.project-memory/tasks/HT-323/` records. After deployment identity and
Cloudflare control-plane readiness pass, add a bounded read-only static
availability admission against that exact immutable URL and the reviewed
manifest. Retry only observed HTTP 404, 500, 502, 503, and 504 responses; each
target gets at most three total attempts, with two seconds between attempts.
All targets share a 120-second deadline. Every accepted response must be HTTP
200 with exact manifest byte count and SHA-256. Fail immediately on 401, 403,
other statuses, network errors, timeouts, redirects, malformed responses, and
any 200 whose size or digest differs. Do not issue a request when the shared
deadline cannot bound it. Never re-publish, fall back to a branch alias, or
emit the existing receipt until every target has passed and the existing final
source/identity checks succeed. Keep receipt schema and `staticByteChecks`
meaning unchanged. Transient observations may contain only bounded attempt,
target index, phase, and HTTP status fields; never include URL or response body.

Keep the standalone read-only `diagnose-static` operation single-pass and
non-authorizing. Add focused tests for a transient allowed status then exact
success, exhausted allowed retries, 401/403 and other statuses without retry,
200 hash/size mismatch without retry, and total-deadline exhaustion without an
extra GET. Preserve the historical publisher fingerprint by normalizing only
the newly reviewed static-read loop to its previous single-pass form; all
unrelated publication orchestration remains byte-pinned. No deploy, publish,
promotion, or production mutation is part of this extension.

## Completed — 2026-10-24 automatic per-user paper recovery

The existing SQLite journal now records each user's desired run state separately
from the backend's observed status. On restart, the backend recovers previously
running Tokyo app-paper sessions after authenticating the unchanged saved
OANDA Practice account. Known legacy shutdown records migrate on upgrade.
Stopped runs stay stopped. A pending Stop can recover quote protection to close
a held paper position, but cannot open another position. Per-user opening
approval still applies. Strategy, calendar, account, instrument or credential
drift blocks recovery and records why; transient authentication failures use
persisted backoff, with eight attempts before manual review. Waiting retries do
not occupy the four authentication slots. Missed entry windows are skipped.
No broker order adapter or global restart switch was added.
